items.title: 11.4 Polar reagents ki taraf alkanes ki ghair-reactive nau'iyat (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 11.4, printed page 252.

blocks.text: Alkanes ya paraffins (Latin parum = thora, affinis = lagao) aam halaat mein acids, alkalis, oxidising aur reducing agents ki taraf inert hain. Un ki reactivity ki kami un ke bonds ki non-polarity se samjhai jati hai: carbon (2.5) aur hydrogen (2.1) ki electronegativities mein khaas farq nahi, to C-H aur C-C bonds ke bonding electrons barabar mushtarka hain, bonds ko taqreeban non-polar aur aam taur par ghair-reactive banate hue. Ghair-reactivity sigma bond ki inertness se bhi samjhai jati hai: us ke electrons nuclei ke darmiyan bohat mazbooti se pakre hote hain, use bohat mustahkam bond banate hue jise torne ke liye bohat energy chahiye. Hydrocarbon ka jalna CO2 paida karta hai, ek greenhouse gas; na-mukammal jalna carbon monoxide aur particulate matter chhorta hai jin ke sehat aur mahol par sangeen asrat hain.

blocks.prompt: Wazahat karein ke alkanes itne mustahkam kyun hain aur addition reactions kyun nahi karte (Quick Check 11.3a; exercise Q.2c).
blocks.explanation: Un ke sab bonds mazboot, non-polar sigma bonds hain jin mein electrophiles ko kheenchne wala electron se bharpoor ilaqa nahi aur nucleophiles ko kheenchne wali polarity nahi, to acids, alkalis aur redox reagents aam darja hararat par unhen chhor dete hain. Addition ko khulne ke liye multiple bond chahiye; alkanes saturated hain, to woh sirf substitution ya thermal tootne se react kar sakte hain.

items: Paraffins ('thora lagao'): acids, alkalis, oxidisers aur reducers ki taraf inert kyunke C-H aur C-C bonds non-polar hain (electronegativity 2.5 vs 2.1) aur sigma bonds mazboot.
